page.layout: One printed page (right-hand page of the opening). Running head centred at top with page number 417 at upper right. Main text in one column of paragraphs, with a heading "De morte principis" and numbered canons. Left margin (outer part of the gutter, from the facing left page) holds several marginal notes in a narrow column, all cut off at the scan edge.

main_text.p: 1 Princeps non facile debet sceptrum deserere, & seipsum imperio abdicare, nisi expresse sentiat se vel ob aetatem, vel ob morbos ad regni gubernacula minus esse idoneum: nec prius se debet abdicare, quam de idoneo successore subditis sit provisum.
2 Subditi abdicationem Principis non temere acceptent, nisi prius certi sint de successore meliori.
3 Abdicatio debet solenniter fieri & per regnum promulgari: idcirco Princeps qui clam aufugit e regno, magnam maculam inurit sibi & regno; sed sibi inprimis.
main_text.head: De morte principis sunt hi Canones:
main_text.p: 1 Magnis cladibus imminentibus Deus auferre solet salutares Principes.
2 Vt boni subditi mortem sui Principis optare non debent, ita mortuum Principem, tanquam patrem amissum acerbe lugere debent, & exequias eius debita magnificentia & pompa celebrare.

p.i: Caeterum mors principis est vel sine relictis liberis; vel talis, post quam liberi relinquuntur.

main_text.head: Mors principis sine liberis relicti, habet hunc Canonem:

p.i: Quo periculosior est status regni nullo haerede relicto, eo magis sollicite cogitandum est & circumspiciendum de idoneo successore.

page.notes: Marginal notes in the left margin are cut off and mostly illegible; only fragments are visible (e.g. "mi-", "non", "ritus", "sub-", "ma-", "mor-", "Ca-", "repit", "incipit", "pri-", "de-", "lefer-", "Prin-"). They are not transcribed. The verse-like numbering of canons and the "Dd" catchword are as printed. Long s rendered as s; Greek abbreviation marks are ordinary ampersands. Page is printed in italic type for the numbered paragraphs.
